problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=(x+2)(2-y).$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)<0?$

feedback.problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=(x+2)(y-1).$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)\le 0?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=-2$ and $y=1.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below. Since we have an "or equal to" inequality, we use solid lines to divide the plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/ce8f784a51d18fd9ea97672b6642b643947845e87b0a4d4c7dd291fcb18f50ed.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/c53a92d71b292288e566db12011c13569ebee65e879598e10b6a14e3acd4f189.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $(x+2)$ | $(y-1)$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-left | $(-3,2)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Top-Right | $(-1,2)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-3,0)$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(-1,0)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |

 

Finally, on our diagram, we shade in the solutions to $f(x,y)\le 0$ using the *last* column of the table above.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/4d65d4c9829b7161152722b7cf6e8605c1cace8078e53430f3480d5d16d74ec4.png)
